title: Covert quiet launch field notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick, low-noise rollout for v2025-02-tokencache: reduce blast radius while validating long-tail latency impact for small tenants. This is a personal-scratchpad plan — not final. Use for pairing w/ on-call and patch crew.

Summary goals:
- Verify KV-cache warmup at production traffic shapes (10–100rps per tenant)
- Detect any 95/99p latency regressions within 3 hours per cohort
- Ensure pinback < 2 minutes from trigger (manual + automated)
- No customer-visible errors > 0.01% across cohorts

Cohorts and schedule:
- T+0 (p0): internal prod-test tenants (5 tenants) — 10m ramp to 2% traffic, 30m observe
- T+1 (p1): low-volume customers (20 tenants) — staggered 5 cohorts, each +1% traffic over 15m windows
- T+2 (p2): selected medium tenants (3 tenants) — individual handoffs, 10% each
- T+3 (p3): open to broader pool if no signals after 4h

Traffic plan & pinning:
- Start traffic split at 1% global; use per-tenant pin to enforce model:v2025-02-tokencache only for cohort.
- Pin command (internal CLI): rwdctl rollout pin --tenant <T> --model v2025-02-tokencache --until 2025-03-05T06:00Z
- Unpin strategy: sequential unpin after 1h stable + green checks OR force-unpin on manual rollback

Observability & SLOs (primary watches):
- 95p latency (gen): baseline 140ms -> alert if +40ms
- 99p latency (gen): baseline 420ms -> alert if +80ms
- Error rate (5xx + model fallback): alert >0.005 absolute increase or >3x relative
- Token cost delta per 1k requests: watch aggregation in billing pipeline

Dashboards & queries to run at T+0:
- kql: service.latency.p95{model:v2025-02-tokencache,region:us-east} by tenant
- trace: look for KV-cache-miss bursts / cold-KV hotpaths
- infra: GPU util per worker, OOM traces, hostOOM counts

Automations & fallback hooks:
- Canary auto-pinback: if p95 > baseline+40ms for 3m across cohort -> auto-reduce to previous model (v2025-01-stable)
- Graceful degrade: route to warmcache variant (v2025-02-tokencache-quantized) if memory pressure high

Manual rollback playbook (cheat-sheet):
1) Confirm signal on dashboard + traces.
2) rwdctl rollout status --model v2025-02-tokencache --cohort <id> (collect logs)
3) rwdctl rollout pin --tenant <T> --model v2025-01-stable --reason "pinback: latency spike"
4) Notify #oncall + #serving-runtime with short summary + link to traces.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want auto-scale-up of worker pool for cohort to hide latency? Pros: reduce observed p99, Cons: hides real regression and costs money.
- Confirm if billing-report latency tags exist for tokencache ops (file issue INF-2356 if not).
- Need a short client-facing FAQ line in case a single-tenant sees poor performance: /FAQ drafts.

Fallback test notes (to run in staging before T+0):
- Simulate KV-cache cold start: sequential cold requests for ten tenant sessions, measure p99 ramp; use load-generator config: loadcfg/cold-kv.json
- Force OOM on a worker and observe autoscaler + fallback routing.

Contacts during launch:
- Primary: Jun Park (pager)
- Backup: Aisha Gomez (pager)
- Infra lead for fast scaling: Ravi Patel

Post-launch checklist (first 6h):
- Collect annotated traces for any p95/p99 deviations
- Export cost delta snapshot (billing-run)
- Confirm no customer tickets opened for related tenants
- Write short one-paragraph summary and folder it under Confluence launch notes

Notes to self: keep the first cohorts tiny and slow. Resist urge to open to p3 until metrics are unambiguously green for 4h. If we see weird tail-latency, suspect KV-cache GC or kernel selection fallback — capture a heap/profile and snap the worker image.

References: linked artifacts above + slack threads #launch-coord (see pinned messages)

--- end scratchpad ---
